passages.note: Assembly floor final passage of SB 100 on 08/28/18, Gabriel in the Ayes; the 44-33 tally is far from near-unanimous.
passages.actor_quote: Ayes Baker, Berman, Bloom, Bonta, Burke, Calderon, Carrillo, Chau, Chiu, Chu, Cooley, Eggman, Friedman, Gabriel

passages.provision_quote: the quantities shall reflect reasonable progress in each of the intervening years sufficient to ensure that the procurement of electricity products from eligible renewable energy resources achieves 25 percent of retail sales by December 31, 2016, 33 percent by December 31, 2020, 44 percent by December 31, 2024, 52 percent by December 31, 2027, and 60 percent by December 31, 2030.
passages.note: Chaptered text of the bill voted on; the operative amendment to Public Utilities Code Section 399.15 raises the renewables procurement requirement on dated deadlines.

rows.reasoning: Gabriel voted Aye on Assembly final passage of SB 100 (2017-2018), whose operative amendment to Public Utilities Code Section 399.15 requires retail sellers to procure eligible renewable energy resources reaching "44 percent by December 31, 2024, 52 percent by December 31, 2027, and 60 percent by December 31, 2030". A renewable-procurement standard with dated targets matches the rung "Require a shift to clean energy through mandates and firm deadlines" clause for clause, and excludes the subsidy and permitting rungs, which the bill does not touch. The chair does not rest on the bill's separate declared policy that "zero-carbon resources" supply 100 percent of retail sales by 2045, which names no energy source; the single-subject energy bill passed 44-33, so the vote is neither multi-subject nor near-unanimous.
